newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: BRATISLAVA, BELGRADE AIM TO BOOST BILATERAL TRADE.
newsitem.headline: BRATISLAVA, BELGRADE AIM TO BOOST BILATERAL TRADE.

text.p: Slovakia and Yugoslavia aim to renew full mutual ties and boost bilateral trade turnover of $400 million for this year, Slovak Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said on Thursday.
"The lifting of United Nations sanctions against Yugoslavia created conditions for the revival of relations between our countries," Meciar told a news conference.
He was speaking after a meeting with Yugoslav Prime Minister Radoje Kontic who arrived in Bratislava on Thursday for an official three-day visit to Slovakia.
"This year we would like our mutual trade to reach a turnover of $400 million, which it was before sanctions were imposed," Meciar said.
"I think this figure is realistic, but at present things are moving slower than we expected," Kontic said. "But we are seeking ways to solve this."
Both premiers said they had discussed possibly setting up a free trade zone between the countries, and were working on an agreement to prevent double taxation.
They said they wanted to create conditions for the the free flow of capital and services and creation of joint ventures.
Meciar said Slovakia fully supported the efforts of Yugoslavia, which now consists of Serbia and Montenegro, to become reintegrated in all international political, social and economic structures.
Kontic said last month's elections in Bosnia were the first step in establishing a firm state structure and carrying out the Dayton peace accords agreed late last year.
The accords led to the lifting of the UN trade sanctions against Yugoslavia.
Kontic said however the large number of refugees displaced by the conflict in former Yugoslavia was a potential threat to peace in the Balkans
Kontic said the international community should help create the economic conditions enabling the roughly two million refugees to return to their homes.
